about.title: Sacramento Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a death in Sacramento is someone else's fault, the family is left carrying two burdens at once: grief, and a set of practical questions nobody wants to ask. Who pays for the funeral? What happens to the income that kept the household going? California law offers one answer through a civil wrongful death claim, which stands apart from any criminal charges the county may pursue. Sacramento recorded 48 traffic deaths in 2025, and public records show the heaviest collision counts along US-50, SR-99, Fruitridge Road and Florin Road, with crashes tending to peak on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. Not every wrongful death claim starts with a crash. Falls, medical errors, defective products and workplace incidents can all qualify. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects Sacramento families with an independent attorney who handles wrongful death cases on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery. A first conversation can clarify who has standing, what losses are recoverable, and how the two-year deadline applies.

items.title: Clarity on Who Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. An attorney can quickly sort out where your family fits.

items.title: Deadlines Explained Early
items.desc: Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is shorter when a city, county or state agency is involved. Knowing this early protects your options.

items.title: A Full Accounting of Losses
items.desc: Recoverable losses go beyond funeral and burial costs to include lost financial support and the loss of love, companionship and guidance. Independent attorneys in our network handle these cases on contingency.

items.question: If the driver who caused the crash is facing criminal charges in Sacramento County, do we still need a civil claim?
items.answer: Yes, the two are separate. A criminal case is brought by the district attorney and focuses on punishment; it does not pay your family for funeral costs, lost support or the loss of companionship. A wrongful death claim is a civil action that your family controls, and it can move forward whether or not criminal charges are filed or result in a conviction.

items.question: Who is allowed to bring a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: The surviving spouse or registered domestic partner and the children come first. If there are none, certain other heirs or people who were financially dependent on the person who died may have standing. Because family situations vary, an attorney can confirm who should be named in the claim.

items.question: Our loved one died in a crash on US-50 or SR-99. Does that change the timeline?
items.answer: It might. The general deadline is two years from the date of death, but if a government entity such as Caltrans, the City of Sacramento or Sacramento County is potentially responsible, a claim usually has to be presented much sooner. That is one reason families are encouraged to speak with an attorney early rather than waiting for the police investigation to close.
